episodes.title: Minimum Description Length Revisited — Peter Grünwald and Teemu Roos

screening.publisher_promise: An up-to-date introduction to and overview of the MDL principle.
screening.screening_reason: The architect of modern MDL sets out learning as compression, with universal codes, the link to Bayes and to frequentist guarantees, and where MDL departs from both. It is the formal backbone behind the repo’s compression claims (Wilson, Ma, Tishby). Rubric: A originator ✓ · B unifying principle ✓ · C derivation ✓ · D 2 · E 2 · F 2.
screening.transcript_question: Which notion of code length makes compression and generalization equivalent, and where does the equivalence break?
screening.caveat: Reading, not a recording; full text on arXiv.

episodes.title: Predictability, Complexity and Learning — Bialek, Nemenman and Tishby

screening.publisher_promise: Defines predictive information, the mutual information between past and future, and relates it to learning and complexity (Neural Computation, 2001).
screening.screening_reason: The originating paper for predictive information, co-authored by Tishby, the user’s exemplar: it connects the sub-extensive part of entropy to model complexity and learning curves. It is the theoretical root of the information bottleneck seminar. Rubric: A originator ✓ · B unifying principle ✓ · C derivation ✓ · D 1 · E 2 · F 2.
screening.transcript_question: How does the divergence of predictive information classify model complexity, and how does that relate to the learning-curve exponents in SLT and statistical physics?
